summary: Whatcom County, WA: a 20-foot L-4 lookout built about 1934 on Mount Baker-Snoqualmie NF; abandoned in 1956 per two sources; footings reportedly remain on an unsigned trail.

facts.status_note: Tower no longer there; a lookout-history website reports, from an undated visit, that all four footings and an anchor point remain
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest)

access.note: Reached by an unsigned, unmaintained trail past the Mount Baker Wilderness sign; no closure is described in the sources read

visit.trail_note: An unsigned trail switchbacks to the right a few minutes past the Mount Baker Wilderness sign, at about 3,800 feet; about three-quarters of a mile on an unmaintained route to the rocky knoll where the lookout once stood

events.note: 20-foot tower with L-4 cab; WillhiteWeb says it was likely built by the CCC
Abandoned in 1956 per firetower.org and firelookout.com; WillhiteWeb says sources differ between 1956 abandonment and removal around 1963
Alternative account in WillhiteWeb only: removed around 1963
Registered April 2, 2020 as US 1960, WA 460; nominated by Tammy McLeod

evidence.supports: tower built on the site in 1934 as a 20-foot tower with L-4 cab; abandoned in 1956 and no longer there
evidence.quote: In 1934 a 20 foot tower with a L-4 cab was built on the site. It was abandoned in 1956 and is no longer there.

evidence.supports: location: Whatcom County and Mt Baker National Forest
evidence.quote: Whatcom County - Mt Baker National Forest - 40N-9E-33

evidence.supports: built around 1934 as a 20-foot L-4 tower, likely by the CCC
evidence.quote: The lookout likely built by the CCC was built around 1934, a 20 foot L-4 tower.

evidence.supports: sources differ between abandonment in 1956 and removal around 1963
evidence.quote: Sources differ whether the site was abandoned in 1956 or removed around 1963.

evidence.supports: not much remains; the usual rusty nails, hinges and glass
evidence.quote: Not much remains today but the usual remains of rusty nails, hinges and glass.

evidence.supports: all four footings and at least one anchor point remain (undated visit)
evidence.quote: All 4 footings remain and at least one anchor point.

evidence.supports: telephone line insulators along the main trail
evidence.quote: Along the main trail on the way up are several telephone line insulators.

evidence.supports: unsigned trail a few minutes past the wilderness sign, at about 3,800 feet
evidence.quote: A few minutes beyond the wilderness sign is an unsigned trail switchbacking to the right (at 3800 feet).

evidence.supports: about three-quarters of a mile up to the rocky knoll where the lookout once stood
evidence.quote: This unmaintained trail goes for three-quarter mile traversing slowly uphill to the rocky knoll where the lookout site was located.

evidence.supports: unsigned trail past the wilderness sign leads to a former lookout site
evidence.quote: which leads to a former lookout site
The lookout is long gone, but will be of interest to lookout buffs.

evidence.supports: registered April 2, 2020, nominated by Tammy McLeod

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firetower.org and firelookout.com say abandoned in 1956. WillhiteWeb says sources differ between abandonment in 1956 and removal around 1963, and does not settle it. The story gives both.

notes_for_editor: Brief record checked and correct (status gone, 2020 registration, elevation 4,115 ft). The brief had the 1934 build right; 1956 abandonment added. Not to be confused with the Goat Mountain lookouts in King, Okanogan or California. The WillhiteWeb site visit is undated, so the footings claim is 'reported' and not dated. The WTA listing corroborates the trail and that the lookout is long gone. No primary Forest Service record checked. Access is public on the sources read; the route is unmaintained. Budget: 1 WebSearch, 5 page reads.
